mainTopic: Inheriting through a grandfather, whether a dead son inherits his mother 'in the grave,' and who must bring proof in two property disputes.
overview: The גמרא first asks whether 'תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך' gives a grandson a real legal claim to inherit his grandfather directly. It tries to prove this from the משנה of a house that fell on a son and his father, but pushes the proof away by reading 'the father's heirs' as the son's brothers. Next, the חכמים ask רב ששת whether a son who died before his mother inherits from her 'in the grave' and passes it to his brothers from his father. רב ששת proves he does not, from a ברייתא about a captive grandfather and his daughter's son. רב אחא בר מניומי brings the same proof from the משנה of a house that fell on a son and his mother. אביי gives the source: the word 'סיבה' links a son to a husband, and a husband does not inherit his wife in the grave. The amud then tells of a sale of 'בר סיסין's property', where רב נחמן and רבא seem to contradict their own rulings in a case about חזקה on a house. The גמרא shows each one is consistent, and the פרק מי שמת ends.

steps.title: Is the verse really meaningless for actual law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea that 'תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך' is only a ברכה and has no legal meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for actual law, does it really mean nothing?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a surprised question about what was just said. It is setting up a proof that will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the פסוק was treated as only a ברכה. That would mean a grandson cannot say 'I come in the power of my father's father.' The גמרא now doubts this and will try to show that in real law a grandson does inherit directly from his grandfather.

keyTerms.meaning: For actual law, for the legal ruling

phrases.english: But with regard to the law, it means nothing?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim that the פסוק is only a ברכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך' is only a ברכה and gives a grandson no claim of his own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rhetorical question that opens the challenge. The proof follows in the next steps.

steps.title: The case of the house that collapsed on son and father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the case of a house that fell on a son and his father, where the father's heirs and the son's creditor argue about who died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A house fell on a man and his father, or on a man and the people he would inherit from. The man owed his wife's כתובה and owed a creditor. The father's heirs say: the son died first, then the father. The creditor says: the father died first, then the son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source about a son and father who died together, so no one knows who died first. Each side claims the order of death that helps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of death matters. If the father died first, the son inherited and his creditor can collect from that property. If the son died first, the son never inherited, so the father's heirs say the creditor has nothing to collect. The next step shows how this helps the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The people he would inherit from

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל אָבִיו,
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: A house fell on him and on his father,
or on him and on those he would inherit from;

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה עָלָיו כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה וּבַעַל חוֹב;
phrases.english: and he owed a wife's כתובה and a creditor;
the father's heirs say:

phrases.aramaic: הַבֵּן מֵת רִאשׁוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הָאָב;
phrases.english: The son died first, and afterward the father died;
and the creditor says:

phrases.aramaic: הָאָב מֵת רִאשׁוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הַבֵּן.
phrases.english: The father died first, and afterward the son died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that backs up the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a grandson inherits from his grandfather in his own right.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of נפל הבית, where the father's heirs and the son's creditor argue about the order of death.

steps.title: If the heirs are the son's sons, the argument only works if grandsons inherit directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'the father's heirs' as the son's own sons. It shows that if grandsons inherited only through their father, the creditor would always win.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't 'the father's heirs' mean the son's sons, and 'those he inherits from' mean his brothers? Now, suppose a grandson cannot say 'I come in the power of my father's father,' because 'תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך' is only a blessing. Then even if the son died first and the father died after, so what? The creditor could tell them: I am taking your father's inheritance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the case is a proof. If the arguing heirs are the son's own sons, their claim only makes sense if they inherit their grandfather directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grandsons inherit only through their father, then the grandfather's property passes through the son no matter who died first. So the creditor could collect either way, and the heirs' claim 'the son died first' would be pointless. Since the source treats the argument as real, grandsons must inherit directly, so the פסוק has legal force.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it true that...? (suggests a reading)
If it enters your mind, if you would think
I come in the power of my father's father (I inherit my grandfather directly)
So what? What difference does it make?

steps.confusionAlert: The grandsons are not claiming through their father here. They are claiming the son never inherited, so the property skips him and comes straight to them. That only works if a grandson inherits his grandfather directly.

phrases.english: What, is it not that 'the father's heirs' are his sons,
phrases.notes: 'His sons' means the sons of the son who died, so they are the grandfather's grandsons.

phrases.english: and 'those he inherits from' are his brothers?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָא מָצֵי אֲמַר
phrases.english: And if you think he cannot say,
'I come in the power of my father's father,'
because when it is written, 'In place of your fathers shall be your sons,'
it is written as a blessing;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מֵת הַבֵּן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת הָאָב –
phrases.english: then when the son died and afterward the father died,
what difference does it make?
Let the creditor say to them:
It is your father's inheritance that I am taking!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the case in step 2 proves the challenge in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a grandson cannot claim 'in the power of my father's father.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'the father's heirs' are grandsons who inherit only through their father, the order of death would not matter and the creditor would always collect. The source treats the order as important, so grandsons must inherit directly.

steps.title: No, the father's heirs are the son's brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading 'the father's heirs' as the son's brothers and 'those he inherits from' as his father's brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'The father's heirs' are his brothers, and 'those he inherits from' are his father's brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by giving a different reading of who the heirs are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the heirs are the son's brothers, they are the father's own sons and clearly inherit him directly. So their argument makes sense without saying anything about grandsons. The case no longer proves that a grandson inherits his grandfather in his own right.
steps.whatToRemember: The case of the collapsed house does not prove that a grandson inherits his grandfather directly. The heirs there can be the son's brothers, who are the father's own children.

phrases.english: No; 'the father's heirs' are his brothers,
and 'those he inherits from' are his father's brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the source that step 3 relied on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this case. It does not decide the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'the father's heirs' are grandsons. They can be the son's brothers, who inherit their father directly, so the case says nothing about grandsons.

steps.title: Can a dead son inherit from his mother and pass it to his paternal brothers?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב ששת whether a son who died before his mother still inherits from her 'in the grave' and passes that inheritance to his brothers from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: If a son dies and then his mother dies, does the son inherit from her while he is in the grave, so that it passes to his brothers from his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks whether a son who has already died can still be treated as his mother's heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the dead cannot inherit. But a mother's property usually goes to her son, and from him to his heirs. If a dead son could inherit 'in the grave,' the mother's property would go to his brothers from his father, even though they are not related to her at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him (a real question, not an attack)
Inheriting while in the grave, after already dying
To pass on as an inheritance
Brothers from the same father (not the same mother)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'brothers from the father' here have a different mother. That is the whole point: if the dead son inherits, his mother's property goes to people who are not her relatives.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּן, מַהוּ שֶׁיִּירַשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר –
phrases.english: A son: what is the law, does he inherit his mother in the grave
phrases.notes: The son died first, and his mother died after him.

phrases.english: to pass it on to his brothers from the father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a son who died before his mother inherits from her in the grave and passes the inheritance to his paternal brothers.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא about captives
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא: a father or son was taken captive and the other died at home, and since no one knows who died first, the heirs of each side split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned it. A father was taken captive and his son died at home, or a son was taken captive and his father died at home. The father's heirs and the son's heirs split.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a ברייתא to answer the question. Here the גמרא only quotes the case; the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases we do not know who died first, so the heirs divide the property. רב ששת will show that this split teaches us the answer to the question.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
A father who was taken captive, and his son died at home;
phrases.notes: The captive also died there, so we don't know who died first.

phrases.english: and a son who was taken captive, and his father died at home –
the father's heirs and the son's heirs divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a son does not inherit his mother in the grave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a captive father or son where the heirs divide.

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot mean a plain father and son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means, because with a regular father and son, the father's heirs and the son's heirs would be the same people.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If we say it is as the ברייתא literally says, who are the father's heirs and who are the son's heirs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the plain reading of the ברייתא. This sets up a new reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man and his son die, the son's heirs are his brothers, and they are also the father's heirs. So there are no two sides to split between. The ברייתא must be talking about a different family relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is as it literally teaches,
who are the father's heirs
and who are the son's heirs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the plain meaning of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'father' and 'son' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a real father and son, both sets of heirs are the same people, so 'divide' makes no sense.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a grandfather and his daughter's son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the 'father' is a maternal grandfather and the 'son' is his daughter's son, so the two sides have different heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: A grandfather was taken captive and his daughter's son died at home, or the daughter's son was taken captive and his mother's father died at home. We don't know who died first, so the grandfather's heirs and the grandson's heirs split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. Now it is about a man and his daughter's son, which gives two different families of heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the grandfather died first, the grandson inherits him, and the money goes to the grandson's father's family. If the grandson died first, the money stays with the grandfather's own heirs. Since no one knows, they split.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this what it means

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what it means:

phrases.aramaic: אָב שֶׁנִּשְׁבָּה וּמֵת בֶּן בִּתּוֹ בַּמְּדִינָה,
phrases.english: a father who was taken captive, and his daughter's son died at home,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁבָּה וּמֵת אֲבִי אִמּוֹ בַּמְּדִינָה,
phrases.english: and his daughter's son who was taken captive, and his mother's father died at home,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ מִית בְּרֵישָׁא –
phrases.english: and we don't know which of them died first –
the father's heirs and the son's heirs divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 7 with a new reading of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a plain father and son.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a maternal grandfather and his daughter's son, so there are two different sets of heirs.

steps.title: If the son inherited in the grave, his side would always win
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת shows that if a dead son inherits his mother in the grave, the grandson's side should get everything either way. Since they split, a son does not inherit in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were true, even if the son died first, he should inherit his mother's father from his grave and pass it to his brothers from his father! So doesn't this prove that a son does not inherit his mother in the grave to pass it to his brothers from the father?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the proof is made. The split in the ברייתא only makes sense if a dead son does not inherit in the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandson's mother, the grandfather's daughter, is no longer alive, so the grandson inherits his grandfather in her place. If a son could inherit his mother 'in the grave,' then even if the grandson died first, he would take her share from the grave and pass it to his paternal brothers, so his side would always win. The ברייתא says they split, so a dead son does not inherit his mother in the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, this proves it

steps.whyThisMatters: This establishes the rule: a son who died before his mother does not inherit from her, and her property does not pass through him to his paternal brothers.

phrases.english: And if it were so,
phrases.notes: If a son really does inherit his mother in the grave.

phrases.english: even granting that the son died first,
let him inherit his mother's father in his grave,
and pass it on to his brothers from his father!
Rather, isn't it true, learn from it –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר,
phrases.english: a son does not inherit his mother in the grave,
to pass it on to his brothers from the father?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, נְהִי נָמֵי דְּבֵן מֵת בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected reading of the ברייתא to answer the question from step 5.
steps.raayaObject: A son does not inherit his mother in the grave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of 'divide' in the captive grandfather and grandson ברייתא.

steps.title: A second proof from the house that fell on a son and his mother
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר מניומי tells אביי that our משנה proves the same thing: when a house falls on a son and his mother, everyone agrees they split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר מניומי said to אביי: We also learned this in our משנה: If the house fell on him and his mother, both sides agree that they divide. If a son inherited in the grave, even if he died first he should inherit his mother and pass it to his paternal brothers! So doesn't this prove a son does not inherit his mother in the grave?
steps.whatsHappening: A second source is brought for the same rule. This time it comes from the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי and בית הלל both agree the heirs split. But if a dead son inherited his mother in the grave, his paternal brothers would always get it all. So the משנה also shows he does not inherit in the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Minyumi said to Abaye,
We too have learned it:
If the house fell on him and on his mother –
these and those agree that they divide.
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִיתָא, נְהִי נָמֵי דְּבֵן מֵת בְּרֵישָׁא,
phrases.english: And if it were so, even granting that the son died first,
let him inherit his mother in his grave,
and let his brothers from his father inherit it!
Rather, isn't it true, learn from it

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר
phrases.english: a son does not inherit his mother in the grave
to pass it on to his brothers from the father?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from the משנה, to the same rule proven in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: A son does not inherit his mother in the grave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (158b): a house fell on a son and his mother, and both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the heirs divide.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: a son does not inherit his mother in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: yes, that is the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by accepting the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the ברייתא and the משנה lead to the same answer. So the question from the beginning is settled: a dead son does not inherit his mother.
steps.whatToRemember: A son who died before his mother does not inherit from her 'in the grave.' So her property never passes through him to his brothers from his father.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אין הבן יורש את אמו בקבר להנחיל לאחין מן האב.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason a son does not inherit his mother in the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just concluded that a son does not inherit his mother in the grave, and now it asks where that rule comes from. This question sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9 to 11 proved from the ברייתא and the משנה that the rule is true. Now the גמרא wants its source in the תורה.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does a son not inherit his mother in the grave? That is what step 11 concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the conclusion reached in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a son does not inherit his mother in the grave.

steps.title: אביי compares a son to a husband through the word 'סיבה'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'סיבה' appears with a son and with a husband. A husband does not inherit his wife in the grave, so a son does not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The word 'transfer' is said about a son, and 'transfer' is said about a husband. Just as with a husband, the husband does not inherit his wife in the grave, so too with a son, the son does not inherit his mother in the grave to pass it on to his brothers from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by linking two cases that share the same word in the תורה. Whatever is true about a husband is also true about a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a husband who dies before his wife cannot inherit her from the grave and pass her property to his own heirs. Because the same word 'סיבה' is used for a son, the son is treated the same way. So a son who died before his mother cannot pass her property to his paternal brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'turning around': an inheritance moving from one tribe to another
Inherits in the grave: a dead relative counted as an heir so he can pass it on

steps.whatToRemember: A son does not inherit his mother in the grave. אביי learns this from the husband through the shared word 'סיבה'.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
'Transfer' was said regarding a son,
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'ולא תסב נחלה' (במדבר 36:7), about an inheritance moving from one tribe to another.

phrases.english: and 'transfer' was said regarding a husband;
just as with 'transfer' said regarding a husband,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבַּעַל יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר,
phrases.english: the husband does not inherit his wife in the grave,
so too with 'transfer' said regarding a son,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר,
phrases.english: the son does not inherit his mother in the grave,
to pass it on to his brothers from the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'סיבה' links a son to a husband. Since a husband does not inherit in the grave, a son does not either.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule from step 11 has a source in the תורה through the shared word 'סיבה'.

steps.title: The sale of 'the property of בר סיסין'
steps.stepSummary: A man sold 'the property of בר סיסין'. One field was called 'of the house of בר סיסין', and the seller claimed it only had that name and was not part of the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his friend: I am selling you the property of בר סיסין. There was one field that was called 'of the house of בר סיסין'. He said to him: This is not really בר סיסין's; it is only called 'of the house of בר סיסין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a brand-new topic: a story about a sale where the buyer and seller argue over one field. The question is whether a field that only carries the name is included in the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller sold 'בר סיסין's property'. One field has that name, but the seller says it was never actually בר סיסין's, so it was not sold. The buyer wants it included.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to his friend:
I am selling you the property of bar Sisin.
There was one piece of land
that was called 'of the house of bar Sisin',

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא לָאו דְּבֵי בַּר סִיסִין הִיא,
phrases.english: he said to him: This is not really of the house of bar Sisin,
phrases.notes: The seller is talking here, trying to keep this field out of the sale.

phrases.english: it is just called 'of the house of bar Sisin'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: נִכְסֵי דְּבַר סִיסִין מְזַבֵּנְינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, not connected to the inheritance discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a dispute: is a field that only carries the name 'בר סיסין' included in a sale of 'בר סיסין's property'?

steps.title: רב נחמן gives the field to the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The case came before רב נחמן, and he left the field in the buyer's hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב נחמן, who placed it in the hands of the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules on the בר סיסין case in favor of the buyer. The field counts as part of the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the seller claims the field only carries the name, רב נחמן does not accept that claim and awards the field to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: He placed it in the hands of

phrases.english: He came before Rav Nachman,
he placed it in the hands of the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אוֹקְמַהּ בִּידָא דְּלוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case told in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The field that is called 'בר סיסין' goes to the buyer.

steps.title: רבא objects: the one taking must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: the rule is that whoever wants to take from another must bring proof, so how can the buyer get the field?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Is this the law?! Whoever takes from his friend must bring the proof!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling using a basic rule of monetary law. He says the buyer should not win without proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field is still in the seller's hands, so the buyer is the one trying to take it. Under 'המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה', the buyer must prove the field was really בר סיסין's. Without proof, it should stay with the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever takes from another must bring proof

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Is this the law?!
Whoever takes from his friend must bring the proof!
phrases.notes: Here the buyer is the one trying to take the field, so רבא says he should have to prove it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: דִּינָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling giving the field to the buyer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer is taking land from the seller, and someone who takes from another must bring proof. The buyer has none, so he should not win.

steps.title: Each אמורא seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction between רבא and another statement of רבא, and between רב נחמן and another statement of רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised a contradiction from רבא against רבא, and from רב נחמן against רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that each of these two אמוראים says the opposite somewhere else, and the next step tells that other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בר סיסין case, רבא sides with the seller and רב נחמן sides with the buyer. The גמרא says another case shows each of them taking the opposite side.

phrases.english: And he contrasted Rava against Rava,
and Rav Nachman against Rav Nachman –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי דְּרָבָא אַדְּרָבָא, וּדְרַב נַחְמָן אַדְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the dispute from step 16 into a challenge against both אמוראים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of both רבא and רב נחמן in the בר סיסין case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each one seems to rule the opposite way in another case, so their positions look inconsistent.

steps.title: The other case: a man in a house claims he bought it
steps.stepSummary: An owner asks a man why he is in his house. The man says he bought it and has lived there for the years of חזקה. The owner answers that he was away in distant settlements.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a certain man said to his friend: What are you doing in this house? He said to him: I bought it from you, and I used it for the years of חזקה. He said to him: I was away in the distant settlements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins telling the other case that shows the contradiction. This is setup: the rulings of רבא and רב נחמן on this case come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, living in a property for the years of חזקה backs up a claim of purchase, because a real owner would have protested. The owner answers that he was far away, so he could not have protested.

keyTerms.meaning: The years of use that back up a claim of ownership

phrases.english: For there was a certain man who said to his friend:
What do you want with this house?
He said to him: I bought it from you,
and I used it for the years of presumed ownership.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא בְּשִׁכּוּנֵי גַּוָּאֵי הֲוַאי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I was in the distant settlements.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ: מַאי בָּעֵית בְּהַאי בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts telling the case that step 17 said would show the contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: someone living in a house claims he bought it and has חזקה, and the owner says he was too far away to protest.

steps.title: רב נחמן tells the occupant to prove his years
steps.stepSummary: The case of the house comes before רב נחמן, and he tells the man living there to prove that he really lived there for the years of חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The occupant came before רב נחמן. רב נחמן said to him: Go prove your years of use.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rules on the house case from step 18. He puts the burden of proof on the man living in the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The occupant claims he bought the house and has lived there long enough for a חזקה. רב נחמן says that claim is not enough by itself, so the occupant must bring witnesses that he really lived there the full time. This is surprising, because the occupant is the one already in the house.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'eating'; here it means using the property during the years of חזקה
Ownership shown by living in or using property for the required years

phrases.english: He came before Rav Nachman,
He said to him: Go clarify your 'eating.'
phrases.notes: 'Eating' means the years you used the house. He is saying: bring witnesses that you really lived there that long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's ruling on the house case presented in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The occupant claiming חזקה must prove that he lived in the house for the full period.

steps.title: רבא objects that the claimant must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן: the one trying to take property from someone else must bring proof, so why should the occupant have to prove anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Is that the law?! Whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling using the basic rule of המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The occupant is the one holding the house, and the owner is trying to take it back. By the standard rule, the owner should have to prove his claim. The occupant should not have to prove his years.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who wants to take from another must bring proof

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Is this the law?!
One who takes from his fellow, the proof is upon him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: דִּינָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the occupant must prove his years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner is the one taking the house away from the occupant, so under המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה the burden of proof should be on the owner, not on the occupant.

steps.title: Both רבא and רב נחמן seem to contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's view here clashes with his view in the בר סיסין case, and so does רב נחמן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty between one statement of רבא and another statement of רבא, and between one statement of רב נחמן and another statement of רב נחמן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up the two cases and shows that each אמורא seems to switch sides. The next two steps will answer each contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בר סיסין case, רב נחמן favored the buyer and רבא favored the seller. In the house case it is reversed: רב נחמן makes the buyer prove his claim, and רבא protects the buyer. Each one seems inconsistent.

phrases.english: Rava is difficult against Rava,
and Rav Nachman against Rav Nachman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the rulings in steps 19-20 with the earlier בר סיסין rulings in steps 15-16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבא and of רב נחמן across the two cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the first case רב נחמן sided with the buyer and רבא with the seller. In the second case רב נחמן sided against the buyer and רבא with him.

steps.title: רבא always follows whoever is in possession
steps.stepSummary: רבא is consistent: in the בר סיסין case the seller held the field, and in the house case the buyer held the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא against רבא is not difficult. Here the seller is standing in his property; there the buyer is standing in his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבא's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא always applies המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה. In the בר סיסין case the seller still held the field, so the buyer had to prove. In the house case the buyer lives there, so the seller must prove. The rule stays the same; only the person in possession changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands in his property, is in possession

phrases.english: Rava against Rava is not difficult:
Here the seller stands in his property,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the בר סיסין field, which the seller still held.

phrases.english: there the buyer stands in his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by who holds the property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא seems to switch between favoring the seller and favoring the buyer.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא always puts the burden of proof on whoever is not in possession.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the sale wording versus an unconfirmed document
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן is consistent too. In the בר סיסין case the field carries that name, so the seller must disprove it. In the house case a חזקה is no better than a שטר, and a שטר must be confirmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן against רב נחמן is not difficult. There, since the seller said 'of the house of בר סיסין' and this field is called 'of the house of בר סיסין', it is up to him to show it is not really theirs. Here, the occupant's claim is no better than holding a document. Wouldn't we tell him: Confirm your document, and then you may stand in the property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רב נחמן's rulings by showing that each case has its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בר סיסין case, the sale wording plainly includes a field with that name. So the seller is the one who must prove it is only a name. In the house case, a חזקה works in place of a sale document. Even someone holding a real שטר must have it confirmed (קיום שטר) before he keeps the property, so the occupant must likewise prove his years.

keyTerms.meaning: A document, here a deed of sale
Confirm your document by verifying its signatures

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים are consistent. רבא always follows who is in possession. רב נחמן looks at what the sale wording implies, and he treats a חזקה claim like a שטר that still needs confirming.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב נַחְמָן אַדְּרַב נַחְמָן לָא קַשְׁיָא –
phrases.english: Rav Nachman against Rav Nachman is not difficult:
Here, since he said to him:
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the בר סיסין case.

phrases.english: 'Of the house of bar Sisin,'
and it is called 'of the house of bar Sisin,'
it rests upon him himself

phrases.aramaic: לְגַלּוֹיֵי דְּלָאו דְּבֵי בַּר סִיסִין הִיא.
phrases.english: to reveal that it is not of the house of bar Sisin.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא דְּנָקֵיט שְׁטָרָא –
phrases.english: Here, let it be no more than if he were holding a document:
phrases.notes: This second 'here' is the house case. His חזקה stands in place of a deed.

phrases.english: Wouldn't we say to him:
Confirm your document, and stand in the property?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב נַחְמָן אַדְּרַב נַחְמָן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by their specific reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן seems to favor the buyer in one case and not in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the בר סיסין case the sale wording favors the buyer. In the house case a חזקה claim is like a שטר, which must be confirmed before the holder can keep the property.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter מי שמת
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the end of פרק מי שמת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, מי שמת.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the argument. It is the standard line said when finishing a chapter, expressing the hope to return to it and learn it again.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who died'
phrases.notes: 'מי שמת' is the name of the chapter, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter מי שמת is completed.
